Definition: Links an entity/process to an attribute or characteristic it possesses. Qualitative property only.
Example: lake HAS_PROPERTY temperature; plants HAS_PROPERTY medicinal

Definition: Links an entity to a functional, ecological, or social role it fulfils.
Example: mountain system HAS_ROLE refuge; species HAS_ROLE pollinator

Definition: Links a property/measurement to its explicitly stated value. Quantitative property only.
Indicates set, taxonomic, population, or categorical inclusion.
Example: Diptera SUBSET_OF insects; endemic species SUBSET_OF regional species
Comment: If we have a species and a group of species, use SUBSET_OF

Definition: Indicates a physical, structural, or compositional part–whole relationship.
Example: leaf PART_OF plant; tributary PART_OF river system
Comment: PART_OF only for a concrete part of the entire object.

Definition:
Indicates the spatial location of an entity within a geographic entity or spatial unit.
Indicates that an organism, population, process, or phenomenon occurs under or within an ecological/environmental context
Example:
Mont Blanc LOCATED_IN European Alps; species LOCATED_IN northern Chile
species LOCATED_IN grassland; plants LOCATED_IN high altitudes
fish LOCATED_IN lake; endemic species LOCATED_IN forest

Definition: Indicates a general, non-specific association between entities or phenomena.
Example:
grassland ASSOCIATED_WITH mountain system;
vicariance ASSOCIATED_WITH biogeographic barriers

Definition: Indicates that an organism, person, or system uses another entity as a resource, substrate, habitat, food, or for another purpose.
Example: Aymara doctors USES medicinal plants; herbivores USES vegetation

Definition: Indicates a causal relationship in which the subject produces or brings about the object.
Example: habitat loss CAUSES decline; predation CAUSES mortality

Definition: Indicates that one entity/process influences or has an effect on another without necessarily asserting causality.
Example: temperature AFFECTS abundance; predators AFFECT insect emergence

Definition: Indicates that the subject facilitates or makes the object/process possible.
Indicates an interaction between two entities, variables, processes, or drivers.
Indicates that the occurrence, magnitude, or state of the subject depends on the object.
Indicates participation of subject in a process, either actively or passively
Indicates that one entity, state, or land-cover type takes the place of another.
Indicates that an entity or feature creates spatial, ecological, or population separation between entities.
Example: ridge SEPARATES valleys; barrier SEPARATES populations

Definition: Indicates an explicitly stated statistical correlation or correlational relationship.
Compares two quantities, magnitudes, rates, effects, or other ordered values and asserts that the first is greater.
Example: [Culicidae abundance LOCATED_IN warmer lakes] GREATER_THAN [Culicidae abundance LOCATED_IN cooler lakes]

Definition: Compares two quantities, magnitudes, rates, effects, or other ordered values and asserts that the first is smaller.
Example: [fish abundance LOCATED_IN acidic lakes] LESS_THAN [fish abundance LOCATED_IN neutral lakes]

Definition: Indicates similarity between entities, properties, communities, patterns, or processes.
Indicates that entities, properties, communities, patterns, or processes are identical
Indicates that two entities, properties, communities, or processes differ.
Links an event, process, state, or phenomenon to a temporal period.
Example: flowering OCCURS_DURING spring; migration OCCURS_DURING April

Definition: Identifies the geographical or conceptual starting point of a movement, lineage, or process.
Identifies the endpoint or destination of a movement or directed process.
Identifies the temporal or sequential starting point of an event/process.
Identifies the temporal or sequential endpoint of an event/process.
Links an observation, finding, pattern, or proposition to a conclusion, implication, or interpretation that it points toward, supports, or provides evidence for.
